general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **US-Iran Conflict:** The United States launched its sixth consecutive night of airstrikes against Iran, targeting critical infrastructure including a railway station, six bridges near Bandar Abbas, and a children's cancer hospital in Ahvaz, resulting in at least eight fatalities and over 400 injuries in Iran. In retaliation, Iran carried out its 13th wave of missile and drone attacks on US military assets and allied nations, striking targets in Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait, Oman, Syria, and Qatar, with reports of damage to a power plant and water desalination stations in Kuwait. This intensified escalation has largely halted civilian and commercial traffic through the crucial Strait of Hormuz, a vital chokepoint for global oil supplies. The widening conflict poses a significant threat to global energy security and regional stability in the Middle East. [Al Jazeera, Reuters, AP News]

• **China's Global AI Governance Initiative:** Chinese President Xi Jinping addressed the 2026 World AI Conference in Shanghai, advocating for a "just and equitable system for global AI governance" and emphasizing that artificial intelligence should not be dominated by any single nation. During his keynote, President Xi unveiled the formation of the China-led World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO), aimed at fostering open-source AI development and providing support to developing countries in this technological domain. This move signals China's ambition to shape international norms and lead global cooperation on AI, potentially influencing future technological standards and geopolitical alliances in the rapidly evolving field of artificial intelligence. [BBC News, Reuters, Al Jazeera]

• **Canadian Wildfires and US Air Quality Crisis:** Dense smoke from ongoing Canadian wildfires generated severe air quality alerts across more than 20 states in the northeastern and upper Midwest United States on July 17, with Detroit, Michigan, recording a hazardous Air Quality Index exceeding 720. The Canadian province of Ontario has requested federal assistance to evacuate residents from remote northern communities heavily impacted by the blazes. This widespread environmental and public health crisis underscores the escalating transnational impact of climate change-exacerbated wildfires on air quality, transportation, and public health infrastructure across North America. [Reuters, AP News]

• **Ukraine Appoints New Prime Minister:** Ukraine's parliament approved Shaki Kureski as the country's new Prime Minister, marking the third such appointment since the commencement of the conflict with Russia. This leadership change is part of a broader government reshuffle aimed at revitalizing Ukraine's foreign policy strategy, advancing efforts to resolve the ongoing conflict, and ensuring the continued operation of critical national infrastructure in preparation for the upcoming winter. The appointment reflects Ukraine's continuous efforts to stabilize its government and adapt its wartime strategy amidst persistent Russian aggression, directly impacting the trajectory of the European security landscape. [NTV]

• **UK Nationalizes British Steel:** The United Kingdom government announced the nationalization of British Steel, a company previously owned by Chinese interests, in a bid to safeguard the nation's domestic steelmaking capacity. This strategic intervention by the UK government reflects concerns over industrial sovereignty and the security of key manufacturing sectors. The nationalization could trigger international trade discussions and signifies a broader trend of governments taking greater control over vital industries amid economic uncertainties and geopolitical shifts. [AP News, Al Jazeera]

Why it matters: The world is currently grappling with a severe convergence of military conflict escalation in the Middle East with global energy implications, intensifying climate change impacts across North America, and major powers vying for leadership in defining the future of critical technologies like artificial intelligence.

investment_markets.title: Markets & Economy
investment_markets.content:
SECTOR ALERTS

*   **Oil & Gas / Energy:** Crude oil prices surged on Friday, with WTI Oil climbing over 4% and posting its largest weekly gain in five months, driven by escalating military tensions between the U.S. and Iran in the Strait of Hormuz. Renewed hostilities and reports of Tehran directing Houthi movements to prepare for a potential closure of the Bab el-Mandeb strait have increased geopolitical risk premiums and concerns over supply disruptions, while tightening global crude inventories and OPEC+ production discipline further supported the rally. This indicates a strong bullish catalyst for Pedro's energy holdings, stemming from fundamental supply concerns and geopolitical instability.

*   **Equities & Indices — Tech / AI (Magnificent 7 excluding Apple):** The broader tech sector, including the Nasdaq 100, saw significant declines as a deep sell-off in semiconductor stocks continued, driven by investor concerns over valuations and a potential slowdown in the AI spending boom. Major tech companies like Microsoft, Alphabet, Nvidia, Meta, and Tesla all experienced drops, with the Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index tumbling over 13% in the past month. This suggests a rotation out of high-flying AI-related names due to valuation reassessment and fears of market overextension, impacting Pedro's tech stock positions.

*   **Equities & Indices — Apple:** Apple's stock defied the broader tech sell-off, hitting a new all-time high and briefly reclaiming its title as the world's most valuable company from Nvidia. This outperformance was fueled by an HSBC analyst upgrade to "buy" with a raised price target of $366, citing Apple's strong product pipeline, strategic AI capabilities with lower capital expenditure compared to hyperscalers, and its ability to leverage its 2.5 billion active device base with "Apple Intelligence". This positive sentiment for Apple, contrasted with the broader tech decline, highlights a flight to perceived quality and strategic AI implementation.

*   **Gold & Silver:** Gold and silver prices continued their monthly downtrend, with gold briefly falling below $4,000/oz and silver dropping over 7% for the week. The decline in precious metals is attributed to rising real interest rates, a stronger U.S. dollar, profit-taking after hitting record highs earlier in 2026, and increasing expectations of a September Federal Reserve rate hike despite intensifying geopolitical conflict in the Middle East. This indicates that hawkish monetary policy expectations are currently overriding safe-haven demand, presenting headwinds for Pedro's commodity positions.

*   **Quantum Computing (QTUM):** The Defiance Quantum ETF (QTUM) experienced a significant monthly decline, although some analysts still see upside potential in quantum computing. The broader market's cautious sentiment towards high-spending AI companies, as seen in the tech sector, may be contributing to the downturn in specialized tech areas like quantum computing, as investors reassess growth projections and capital expenditure. This could signal a re-evaluation of speculative growth sectors.

Why it matters: The market is undergoing a significant rotation where geopolitical tensions are boosting energy prices, while hawkish Fed expectations and valuation concerns are causing a broad sell-off in the tech sector, with Apple standing out as a defensive growth play due to its strategic AI approach and disciplined capital expenditure.

eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
• **Commission Measures for the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR):** The European Commission adopted delegated and implementing acts on July 13, 2026, to refine the scope and operational aspects of the EUDR. Previously, a broader range of products required due diligence for deforestation-free sourcing. Now, cattle hides, skins, leather, re-treaded tyres, soybeans for sowing, articles of vulcanised rubber, conveyor and transmission belts, and aircraft and motor vehicle seats are explicitly removed from the Regulation's scope. Conversely, soluble coffee, certain palm oil derivatives, and frozen cattle tongues are added, with compliance for these new additions commencing on December 30, 2027. An updated Information System to support implementation is also operational. This provides greater clarity for businesses involved in these commodity supply chains, impacting compliance requirements and offering a preparation period for newly included products, including Portuguese enterprises in the affected sectors.

• **Temporary €3 Customs Duty on Low-Value Parcels:** From July 1, 2026, the EU has introduced a temporary €3 customs duty on low-value parcels imported from outside the EU, primarily affecting e-commerce. Previously, many low-value parcels (up to €150) were often exempt from customs duties. Now, this duty applies to a wide range of products commonly bought online, such as clothing, toys, and electronics, when their value is up to €150. This regulation entered into application this week. This directly impacts the cost of online purchases from non-EU countries for EU consumers and introduces a new financial and administrative burden for e-commerce businesses and logistics operators, including those serving the Portuguese market.

• **Regulation (EU) 2026/1384 on Steel Market & Global Overcapacity:** This Regulation entered into application on July 1, 2026, introducing a revised tariff-rate quota (TRQ) system for steel imports. Previously, the system offered less flexibility regarding unused quotas. Now, the new rules aim to address global overcapacity by reducing import quotas and imposing higher duties on imports exceeding these quotas. It also provides greater flexibility for economic operators by allowing the carry-over of unused quotas from one quarter to the next, but only within the same year. This directly affects steel importers and downstream industries across the EU, including those in Portugal, potentially leading to adjustments in sourcing and increased costs for certain steel products.

• **Council Decision (CFSP) 2026/1780 amending Restrictive Measures concerning Ukraine:** On July 17, 2026, the Council formally approved Decision (CFSP) 2026/1780. Previously, specific restrictive measures under Decision 2014/145/CFSP targeted actions undermining or threatening Ukraine's territorial integrity, sovereignty, and independence. Now, this Decision amends the existing framework, likely by updating the list of sanctioned individuals and entities or modifying the scope of these restrictive measures. This requires businesses and financial institutions in Portugal and across the EU to ensure ongoing compliance with updated sanctions lists, affecting potential transactions and relationships.

Why it matters: This week saw the entry into application of new trade measures impacting both e-commerce and industrial sectors, alongside specific adjustments to environmental regulations and updates to foreign policy sanctions, collectively shaping the operational landscape for EU businesses and consumers.

ai_productivity.title: ⚡ AI & Productivity
ai_productivity.content:
• **Moonshot AI:** Kimi K3, an open-source large language model with approximately 2.8 trillion parameters, shipped on July 16, 2026, marking a significant entry into the frontier AI space. This model, noted for its lower costs, ranks third overall on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (scoring 57, ahead of Claude Opus 4.8) and has topped AI coding leaderboards. Developers can now leverage a highly capable, open-source model for coding tasks and advanced text generation with competitive performance, especially for projects seeking cost-effectiveness or customizability, for example, autonomously generating complex code snippets or performing multi-turn reasoning within an application at a reduced operational cost.

• **Anthropic:** Claude Code received a broad stability and quality update on July 16, 2026, and now defaults to using Claude Opus 4.8 on Bedrock, Vertex, and AWS. Claude Opus 4.8 is a capstone upgrade to the Claude 4 line, offering faster thinking modes at one-third the cost of its predecessor, Opus 4.7, for comparable quality. Developers using Claude Code benefit from a more stable environment and the enhanced reasoning and coding capabilities of Opus 4.8 by default, enabling them to tackle more complex programming tasks and multi-step agentic workflows directly within their IDEs or CLIs with improved reliability.

• **Figma:** On July 16, 2026, Figma Make shipped with integrated GPT-5.6 and the ability to run multiple AI image edits concurrently. This enhancement provides designers with more sophisticated AI-powered content generation and streamlines visual iteration by allowing background processing of image modifications while continuing design work. Designers can rapidly iterate on visual concepts by generating AI-powered images and modifying them in parallel, for example, prompting Figma Make to create several variations of an icon or header image based on text descriptions and then continuing to work on the layout while the AI processes edits in the background.

• **Cursor:** Improvements to Cursor in Slack shipped on July 17, 2026, enabling the AI coding assistant to share task plans upfront, operate effectively in multi-repository environments, and manage workflows across multiple Slack channels and threads. This update significantly enhances collaborative development by providing better transparency and contextual awareness for AI-assisted tasks within Slack. Development teams can better coordinate and track AI-assisted coding tasks directly within their Slack workspace, for instance, assigning a bug fix to a Cursor agent that will outline its approach, access necessary code across different repos, and post updates in relevant discussion threads without manual intervention.

Why it matters: The rapid advancements in open-source frontier models and the deeper integration of AI capabilities into core productivity tools are fundamentally reshaping how developers and knowledge workers approach complex tasks, enabling more autonomous and collaborative workflows.

portugal_policy.title: 🇵🇹 Portugal Policy & Law
portugal_policy.content:
• **Portaria n.º 298/2026/1 – Alterações à Declaração Periódica do IVA:** Aprova novos modelos para a declaração periódica do Imposto sobre o Valor Acrescentado (IVA), seus anexos e instruções de preenchimento. Previamente, os modelos de declaração não integravam explicitamente as particularidades do regime de grupos de IVA nem as regularizações específicas introduzidas pelo Pacote Habitação. Agora, os novos modelos incluem campos para acomodar o regime de grupos de IVA (instituído pela Lei n.º 62/2025) e as regularizações de IVA relacionadas com a legislação do Pacote Habitação (Decreto-Lei n.º 97/2026), designadamente as relativas à aplicação da taxa reduzida para determinadas construções habitacionais (verba 2.42 da Lista I). A parte das alterações referente ao regime de grupos de IVA e às regularizações do Pacote Habitação entrou em vigor a 1 de julho de 2026, enquanto as restantes alterações nos modelos terão efeitos a partir de 1 de julho de 2027. O impacto prático é que as empresas que operam sob o regime de grupos de IVA e aquelas envolvidas em projetos de habitação com taxas de IVA reduzidas deverão utilizar os formulários de declaração atualizados para assegurar a conformidade fiscal.

• **Portaria n.º 301-A/2026 – Atualização da Taxa do Imposto Sobre os Produtos Petrolíferos e Energéticos (ISP) para Gasóleo Profissional:** Atualiza a taxa do ISP aplicável ao gasóleo profissional. Com o aumento anunciado do preço do gasóleo, a taxa de ISP será diminuída em aproximadamente €0.0178/litro. A regra anterior previa um montante de reembolso aos transportadores por via do gasóleo profissional de cerca de €0.1746/litro (em vigor até 5 de julho). A nova portaria ajusta este valor de reembolso, que entrará em vigor a 20 de julho de 2026. O impacto prático é uma redução na carga fiscal para as empresas de transporte que utilizam gasóleo profissional, através de um maior reembolso, visando mitigar o impacto do aumento dos preços dos combustíveis.

• **Lei n.º 31/2026 – Alargamento do Serviço de Assistência Pessoal de Apoio à Pessoa com Deficiência ou Incapacidade:** Estabelece o alargamento do serviço de assistência pessoal no âmbito do Modelo de Apoio à Vida Independente (MAVI). Anteriormente, o acesso a estes serviços podia estar sujeito a comparticipações familiares ou verificação de condição de recursos. A nova lei garante a gratuitidade do acesso a esta resposta social, eliminando o pagamento de comparticipação familiar e a verificação de condição de recursos do destinatário ou do seu agregado familiar. Além disso, determina que o Governo deve promover o aumento da capacidade existente em 30% no primeiro ano de execução da lei, através de novos acordos de cooperação e do aumento de horas disponibilizadas aos Centros de Apoio à Vida Independente (CAVI). Esta lei foi publicada a 14 de julho de 2026, entrando em vigor a 15 de julho de 2026. O impacto prático é a melhoria significativa no apoio à vida independente para pessoas com deficiência, através do acesso gratuito e alargado a serviços essenciais.

• **Decretos da Assembleia da República – Reformas no Sistema de Justiça Criminal e Transposição de Diretiva Europeia:** O Presidente da República promulgou dois decretos da Assembleia da República que visam reformar o sistema de justiça criminal. Um dos decretos altera o Código de Processo Penal, o Código Penal e o Regulamento das Custas Processuais, atualizando e aperfeiçoando normas processuais e penais. O outro decreto procede à transposição da Diretiva (UE) 2024/1260, relativa à recuperação e perda de bens, fortalecendo os instrumentos legais para combater a corrupção e a criminalidade organizada transfronteiriça. Anteriormente, as disposições legais nestas áreas seguiam os quadros jurídicos existentes. Estes decretos foram promulgados a 17 de julho de 2026, com entrada em vigor esperada após a sua publicação em Diário da República. O impacto prático é o reforço da eficácia e celeridade do sistema judicial, com novas ferramentas para o combate à criminalidade, afetando os procedimentos legais para cidadãos e empresas.

Why it matters: A combinação de alterações fiscais, como as novas regras para a declaração de IVA e a redução do ISP para o gasóleo profissional, juntamente com o alargamento do apoio a pessoas com deficiência e as reformas no sistema de justiça criminal, reflete um esforço do Governo para impactar diretamente tanto o ambiente de negócios quanto a proteção social em Portugal.

us_policy.title: 🇺🇸 United States Policy
us_policy.content:
• **USTR Imposes 25% Section 301 Tariffs on Brazilian Goods:** On July 15, 2026, the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) announced a final 25% tariff on specific imports from Brazil, effective July 22, 2026. This action concludes a Section 301 investigation into Brazil's unfair trade practices, including digital trade, preferential tariffs, insufficient intellectual property protections, lack of reciprocal ethanol market access, and illegal deforestation. Previously, these goods were not subject to this specific 25% tariff; now they will be, in addition to a 10% tariff under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, which is set to expire on July 24, 2026. This trade action will likely increase the cost of affected Brazilian goods for U.S. importers and consumers, potentially leading to shifts in supply chains and retaliatory trade measures.

• **DHS Eliminates "Duration of Status" for F, J, and I Nonimmigrants:** On July 17, 2026, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) published a final rule in the Federal Register, effective September 15, 2026, changing the admission period for F (academic student), J (exchange visitor), and I (media) nonimmigrants from "duration of status" (D/S) to a fixed period of admission, generally not exceeding four years plus a 30-day grace period. Previously, these nonimmigrants were admitted for an unspecified D/S tied to their program length; now, they will receive an I-94 with a specific "admit until" date and must apply for an extension of stay (EOS) with U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) for additional time. The F-1 post-completion grace period is shortened from 60 days to 30 days. This rule significantly alters the regulatory landscape for international students and exchange visitors, potentially impacting U.S. educational institutions and the influx of foreign talent.

• **Department of State Designates Juárez Cartel and Los Viagras as Foreign Terrorist Organizations:** On July 16, 2026, the U.S. Department of State formally designated two Mexican criminal groups, the Juárez cartel (also known as La Línea) and Los Viagras, as Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs). Previously, these groups were not officially designated as FTOs. This designation significantly increases criminal, civil, and compliance risks for companies and individuals providing "material support" to these organizations under various U.S. laws, including the Anti-Terrorism Act and economic sanctions laws. This escalates the U.S. government's efforts to combat transnational criminal organizations, requiring heightened due diligence and compliance measures for businesses operating in regions affected by these groups.

• **DOE Finalizes Procedures for Defense Production Act Voluntary Agreements:** On July 17, 2026, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) adopted an interim final rule, published on August 25, 2025, as a final rule, establishing procedures for developing and carrying out voluntary agreements and plans of action under the Defense Production Act (DPA). This rule is effective on July 17, 2026. Previously, these procedures were governed by an interim final rule; now, they are formalized into a final rule, providing a defense from antitrust laws when certain criteria are met. This streamlines the process for private entities to collaborate with the government on national defense and emergency preparedness, potentially enhancing supply chain resilience in critical sectors.

Why it matters: The Department of Homeland Security's final rule ending "duration of status" for nonimmigrant students and exchange visitors represents a fundamental shift in U.S. immigration policy with broad implications for international education and talent mobility.
